**Direct answer:** No one has walked on Mars, so there was no "first human" on its surface. The question rests on a false premise. Only robotic spacecraft have operated there.

Claims and supporting sources:

- No human has walked on Mars, and no crewed Mars mission is currently funded or scheduled.
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_crewed_Mars_mission_plans
  - https://marsprogress.com/

- Only robots are at Mars now: two rovers on the ground and six orbiters.
  - https://marsprogress.com/

- NASA's stated goal is to send astronauts to Mars in the 2030s, with no firm date. Other sources say the early 2040s, or a delay to about 2039.
  - https://theconversation.com/nasa-wants-to-send-humans-to-mars-in-the-2030s-a-crewed-mission-could-unlock-some-of-the-red-planets-geologic-mysteries-239814
  - https://www.universetoday.com/articles/2033-is-the-perfect-year-to-send-humans-to-mars-with-a-bonus-venus-flyby

- NASA's 2022 objectives describe a 30-day, two-person surface mission. Other estimates involve much longer stays.
  - https://www.space.com/nasa-plans-astronauts-mars-mission-30-days
  - https://interestingengineering.com/science/nasa-releases-50-key-objectives-to-tackle-on-its-first-human-mission-to-mars

- SpaceX had floated a 2028 crewed flight. In February 2026 it reportedly told investors it would prioritize the Moon, which cancelled the uncrewed 2026 Mars landing plan.
  - https://marsprogress.com/

**Caveats:** The search summaries I relied on were a mix of dated and recent. I read only the search results, not the full pages. The SpaceX report is secondhand (attributed to the Wall Street Journal), and I didn't check it against the original. Several of the NASA timeline sources are one to four years old.
